title: Vertile AI IaC Manifest Schema
summary: The iac.json manifest is the source of truth for app infrastructure intent, provider reconciliation, and environment metadata wiring.

sections.title: Manifest Identity
sections.summary: Every manifest declares its schema version and project identity before provider or app configuration.

fields.description: Schema version. Current manifests use version 1.
Human-facing project identity used by generated infrastructure and documentation.
Logical environment names or environment objects with file-selection metadata.

sections.title: Provider Configuration
sections.summary: Provider blocks hold provider-specific configuration that cannot be expressed portably yet.

fields.description: Vercel team slug used by Vercel env, project, and domain reconciliation.
Maps Vercel targets such as preview and production to logical IaC environments.
Default Vercel automation-bypass operation for every managed Vercel project. Use ensure for repeatable note-keyed sync.
Default Vercel project settings applied to every deployable Vercel app.
Provider deployment map from stage names such as uat or prod to logical environments and provider-specific render inputs.
GitHub Actions environment, variable, and secret publishing configuration.

sections.title: Vercel Automation Bypass
sections.summary: Automation bypass is project protection configuration, not an application runtime environment variable.

fields.description: Repeatable operation. Vertile IaC exact-matches note against Vercel-exposed automation-bypass notes, then sends update when the note exists or generate when it does not.
Direct Vercel generate operation. Use for explicit provisioning or rotation, not ordinary recurring sync.
Direct Vercel update operation for a known existing secret.
Direct Vercel revoke operation for a known existing secret.
Per-project override. Set false to opt a Vercel project out of the provider-level automation-bypass default.

sections.title: Applications
sections.summary: Apps are deployable application surfaces. Provider adapters map app fields to provider-specific projects and settings.

fields.description: Stable app identifier used by env sync, provider manifests, and project reconciliation.
Provider project id, commonly the Vercel project id for Vercel reconciliation.
App root used by Vercel project settings and env file output.
Domains assigned to this app by provider domain reconciliation.

sections.title: Object Storage
sections.summary: Object storage is a portable bucket intent. DigitalOcean renders Spaces buckets and exposes non-sensitive connection metadata as Terraform outputs.

fields.description: Stable object-storage identifier used in generated Terraform resource and output names.
Defaults to private. DigitalOcean maps public to the public-read ACL.
Optional DNS-safe bucket name: 3-63 lowercase letters, digits, or dashes.
Optional lowercase DigitalOcean region slug; otherwise the selected deployment or provider region is used.
Optional explicit DigitalOcean Spaces canned ACL.
Non-sensitive bucket connection metadata. Access keys are never emitted.

sections.title: Services
sections.summary: Services describe long-running app processes. v1 supports public container services, with DigitalOcean rendering one secure empty Droplet host per service.

fields.description: Stable service identifier. Keys must be unique and must not collide after Terraform name sanitization.
Optional reference to an apps[].key.
v1 supports container-backed long-running services only.
Internal application/upstream port from 1 to 65535. DigitalOcean firewalls do not expose this port publicly.
Defaults to true. v1 rejects false.
Defaults to 1. v1 rejects any value other than 1.
Absolute health path beginning with /. Rendered as rollout metadata and a Terraform output when set.
Rejected in v1. Reverse proxy protocol handling belongs to the consumer release pipeline.
Defaults to droplet. v1 rejects any other DigitalOcean service mode.
DigitalOcean region. Resolution order is service override, selected deployment region, then provider region; one source is required for service rendering.
Droplet size. First-class services default to s-1vcpu-2gb.
Droplet image. Defaults to ubuntu-24-04-x64.
Droplet backups flag. Defaults to true.
Droplet monitoring flag. Defaults to true.
Defaults to true. v1 rejects false because public services require a stable Reserved IP.
DigitalOcean SSH key fingerprints for host access. Omit unless management access is intentionally configured.
Explicit SSH allowlist. Empty, duplicate, invalid, or global CIDRs are rejected; SSH ingress is omitted when unset.

sections.title: DigitalOcean Backend And Outputs
sections.summary: DigitalOcean uses local Terraform state by default, can render an optional Spaces S3-compatible backend for selected deployments, and exposes stable non-sensitive output JSON.

fields.description: DigitalOcean Terraform provider version. Defaults to 2.96.0 and may be overridden by deployment version.
Optional remote state backend type. Only spaces is supported.
Pre-created Spaces bucket for Terraform state. The CLI does not create the state bucket.
Lowercase DigitalOcean region slug used in the Spaces endpoint.
Defaults to true. true renders Terraform ~> 1.11 with use_lockfile; false renders Terraform >= 1.6.3 without use_lockfile.
Rejected. Use AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables for Spaces backend credentials.
Required when a Spaces backend is configured and that deployment is selected. Must be a safe relative object key.
Stable JSON envelope for non-sensitive Terraform outputs. The command initializes the selected rendered workspace before reading terraform output -json.
Stable service output names for release automation, alongside droplet_id, reserved_ip, and public_host.

sections.title: Environment Metadata
sections.summary: Env metadata is authored in iac.json and drives local package env sync, Vercel env sync, and GitHub Actions env publishing.

fields.description: Root directory for env source files. Defaults to .vertile-iac/env.
Package/app keys included in local env projection.
Structured metadata for env keys, including example, optional .env.example descriptions, encrypted, browser, package routing, and environment include/exclude rules.
